Subject: Deployment path options - latency & throughput profile (post-call recap)

Hi Tanya — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have the same picture before we loop in Procurement and Solutions:

Summary of requirements (from call):
- Target inference tail latency: p95 <= 70ms (hard constraint for product feature)
- Steady throughput: ~700 req/s; occasional bursts up to ~1.2k req/s for short periods (2–5 min)
- Request size: typical prompt ~600 tokens; context window rarely exceeds 2k tokens
- Data: customer PII not stored long-term; preference for Private VPC for auditability but open to Hosted if we can meet latency/SLA

Immediate ask from our side:
1) Confirm whether 70ms p95 is strict for all regions or only US production.
2) Share any procurement timelines or PO templates so we can align on pricing cadence.
3) Any regulatory constraints that would mandate on-prem or VPC-only?

Initial thoughts (non-binding): based on throughput + tight p95 target, Dedicated capacity is likely the best fit for predictable tail latency and isolation; Hosted API could be considered if you want faster time-to-market and are flexible on burst/latency SLOs. Neha will follow up with a capacity sketch and preliminary cost ranges.

Attachments: olive_requirements_v1.pdf (copied from your doc)

Proposed next step: 30-minute architecture review with our Solutions team to validate the performance envelope and sizing. Are you available Thu, Aug 6 10:00–10:30am PT?

Thanks,
Marcus Lin

marcus@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0183

Thanks Marcus — appreciate the recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- The 70ms p95 target is for customer-facing inference in US prod only; EU will tolerate higher p95 (~150ms) for now.
- The 700 req/s steady number is our conservative baseline; we expect 700–900 during normal peak hours and spikes to 1.2k for marketing-driven campaigns (bursts ~3–7 minutes).
- We prefer a Private VPC deployment ideally, but that adds procurement time. If Hosted offers guaranteed p95 and predictable cost, we'd consider it.
- Cost sensitivity: monthly budget target for inference is ~$30k–$45k depending on measured latencies and SLO credits.

Procurement note: we typically need a 45-day lead time for any vendor contract; can you share an indicative SOW or pricing bands to feed to procurement?

Happy to do Aug 6 at 10am PT for the architecture review — Dan will join to cover infra constraints.

Tanya — thanks for the detail. Quick technical readout to help the architecture review and to give Procurement something tangible. High-level recommendations below; details in attached spreadsheet (initial_capacity_costs.xlsx).

Option A — Redwood Dedicated (recommended):
- Rationale: predictable GPU isolation gives more stable p95 and predictable scaling for sustained 700–900 req/s. Dedicated pools let us reserve capacity and enforce lower tail latency (we can hit ~40–60ms p95 on typical models with the right instance class and batching).
- Suggested baseline: 2x medium Dedicated GPU pools (N+1 for failover) sized for sustained 900 req/s with autoscale headroom to 1.5k.
- Scaling: autoscale policy at 70% CPU/KV-cache hit thresholds; burst buffer to handle 1.2k short bursts without queuing impact.
- Monitoring & observability: per-route p95, cold-starts, KV cache hit rate, token-cost breakdown.
- Pros/cons: Pros = strong p95, predictable unit economics; Cons = longer lead + commit needed for best pricing.

Option B — Hosted API (fastest to ship):
- Rationale: no infra commitment; ideal for short pilots.
- Caveats: multi-tenant noise; p95 can vary under platform pressure. We can prioritize your traffic via routing tiers for a premium but that still has different SLO characteristics than Dedicated.
- Feasibility: to meet 70ms p95 in US you likely need higher cost tiering and reserved concurrency; not impossible but cost may exceed your stated budget.

Private VPC / On-prem:
- Can satisfy audit/VPC constraints but requires more lead time and support; we'd need to scope network egress and KMS.

Preliminary cost note (ballpark):
- Dedicated baseline (2 pools + autoscale): $28k–$42k/mo depending on instance sizing and committed term.
- Hosted approach to hit p95: likely >$40k/mo with premium routing.

Next steps I recommend for the Aug 6 call:
1) Share a few representative traffic traces (1–2 hours) so we can model batching and KV cache hit rates.
2) We’ll run a short synthetic load run against a hosted preflight to estimate p95 under your prompt distribution.
3) If you prefer Dedicated, I’ll prepare a firmed sizing + pricing worksheet for Procurement.

Attachment: initial_capacity_costs.xlsx

-Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.com
